stresses: HOMEOWNER CROSSTALK / ATTRIBUTION, three separate instances: (1) the homeowner asserts a furnace efficiency ("ninety-five percent") the auditor explicitly declines to take on faith ("I hear you, but I need to read the plate myself") before independently confirming furnace + fuel from the plate -- and the efficiency number itself has no write target regardless (HAZARD 4); (2) the homeowner offers a move-in date/derived age ("about ten years old ... twenty-fifteen") as a proxy for equipment year, which the auditor explicitly refuses to log absent a readable plate -- declared_absent, never 2015 or any derived year; (3) the homeowner relays second-hand hearsay asbestos ("the previous owners told us"), which the auditor neither confirms nor denies but states plainly was never tested -- the health-matrix explicit-non-performance pattern (Not Tested), on a leaf a careless model might stamp Failed purely off hearsay. Also exercises the schema-forced hvacSystemEquipmentType/shared-ducts axis ambiguity, a completed ambient-CO test read as Passed ('CO test right by the two appliances ... zero' -- textually the corpus's clearest instance of the ambient-vs-undiluted-flue-CO confusability, see RECONCILIATION.md ruling 4; resolved to healthAmbientCarbonMonoxide because neither the flue nor a probe nor combustion gas is named), and a closing blanket deferral ('the rest of the shell') scoped to the shell named set -- this transcript is disclaimer-policy.mjs's own citation for that named set.

arguable.note: SCHEMA FINDING, not a transcript ambiguity. The auditor states the equipment's identity and fuel after independently reading the plate ("it's a furnace, natural gas") but says nothing about cooling either way, so the ducts-sharing-with-AC axis hvacSystemEquipmentType conflates onto the same enum is left completely unaddressed. Per ANNOTATOR_GUIDE.md rule 6's mechanical tie-break, `member` is "Furnace with standalone ducts" because it appears first in schema.ts's enum-list order (index 2 of 17 vs. "Furnace / Central AC (shared ducts)" at index 16), not because it is a more likely reading.

arguable.note: A CROSSTALK TRAP. The homeowner claims (second-hand, from previous owners) that asbestos is present in the basement. The auditor explicitly says he has not tested for it himself and it wasn't in scope today. The correct reading is 'Not Tested' (an explicit, addressed non-performance), never 'Failed' -- a model that reports 'Failed' here is treating unconfirmed homeowner hearsay as the auditor's own tested finding, the exact hallucination this leaf is built to catch (parallel to the worked example's ambient-CO trap). A model that leaves this leaf null is a milder, acceptable miss; 'Failed' (or 'Passed') is the serious wrong answer, hence acceptableAlternatives is empty.

notes.hvac.hvacHeatingSystemModel: Only the manufacturer (Goodman) is ever stated; no model number or name is given. Genuinely empty leaf, not a dropped value.
notes.hvac.hvacHeatingSystemModelYear: The homeowner's move-in date ("we bought the house in twenty-fifteen") and derived age ("about ten years old") are explicitly rejected by the auditor as not the equipment date ("that's your move-in date, not the equipment date, and I'm not going to log that as the equipment year unless the plate confirms it") -- the template case for never attributing a second speaker's unconfirmed number to the auditor's own assertion. Not recorded as 2015, 2016, or any derived year.
notes.basedata.yearBuilt: "we bought the house in twenty-fifteen and it was brand new then" is spoken entirely in service of the EQUIPMENT-year question, and the auditor's reply addresses only the equipment date, never the house's construction year as its own topic -- he neither confirms nor uses this figure himself. Per rule 3's attribution rule (a second speaker's statement becomes a value only if the auditor independently confirms it in their own words), this is left unmentioned rather than yearBuilt: 2015; the auditor's silence on this axis is not an independent confirmation.
notes.dhw: "natural draft up the flue" (the water heater's venting mechanism) has no corresponding leaf in DhwFields (no DHW vent-type field exists in the 51-leaf set) -- deliberately excluded, not missed, per rule 9.
notes._general: The homeowner's opening line ("the installer said ninety-five percent when he put it in") is a spoken AFUE efficiency figure, HAZARD 4 in schema.ts: there is deliberately no efficiency capture field, and it is also unconfirmed homeowner speech never adopted by the auditor in his own words, so it is excluded for two independent reasons. hvac.hvacUpgradeAction is never stated (recommendations are explicitly deferred: "We'll get to recommendations at the end" -- and the transcript ends before any are given), so it stays unmentioned despite being one of the two API-required leaves. Wall, window, and the rest of attic beyond what's mentioned here are entirely deferred by the closing 'shell' disclaimer.
